মানসিক দক্ষতা.question: ১০৬) 2021 সালের 5 জানুয়ারি মঙ্গলবার হলে, একই বছরের 20 ফেব্রুয়ারি কী বার ছিল?
মানসিক দক্ষতা.exp:
প্রশ্ন: 2021 সালের 5 জানুয়ারি মঙ্গলবার হলে, একই বছরের 20 ফেব্রুয়ারি কী বার ছিল?

সমাধান:
2021 সাল একটি সাধারণ বছর। তাই জানুয়ারি মাসে দিন = 31 দিন।
5 জানুয়ারি থেকে 31 জানুয়ারি পর্যন্ত দিনের ব্যবধান = 31 - 5 = 26 দিন

এরপর 1 ফেব্রুয়ারি থেকে 20 ফেব্রুয়ারি পর্যন্ত = 20 দিন

সুতরাং মোট দিনের ব্যবধান = 26 + 20 = 46 দিন

এখন,
46 ÷ 7 = 6 সপ্তাহ, ভাগশেষ 4 দিন

অর্থাৎ, 5 জানুয়ারি মঙ্গলবারের 4 দিন পর হবে 20 ফেব্রুয়ারি।

মঙ্গলবার → বুধবার = 1 দিন
বুধবার → বৃহস্পতিবার = 2 দিন
বৃহস্পতিবার → শুক্রবার = 3 দিন
শুক্রবার → শনিবার = 4 দিন

∴ 2021 সালের 20 ফেব্রুয়ারি ছিল শনিবার।

সঠিক উত্তর: ক) শনিবার

মানসিক দক্ষতা.question: ১০৫) পরস্পর সংযুক্ত দুটি গিয়ারের মধ্যে ছোট গিয়ারের দাঁত 20টি এবং বড় গিয়ারের দাঁত 40টি। ছোট গিয়ার 2 বার ঘুরলে বড় গিয়ার কতবার ঘুরবে?
মানসিক দক্ষতা.exp:
প্রশ্ন: পরস্পর সংযুক্ত দুটি গিয়ারের মধ্যে ছোট গিয়ারের দাঁত 20টি এবং বড় গিয়ারের দাঁত 40টি। ছোট গিয়ার 2 বার ঘুরলে বড় গিয়ার কতবার ঘুরবে?

সমাধান:

পরস্পর সংযুক্ত দুটি গিয়ারের ক্ষেত্রে,
ছোট গিয়ারের ঘূর্ণন সংখ্যা × ছোট গিয়ারের দাঁত সংখ্যা = বড় গিয়ারের ঘূর্ণন সংখ্যা × বড় গিয়ারের দাঁত সংখ্যা

ধরি, বড় গিয়ারটি = x বার ঘুরবে।

প্রশ্নমতে,
2 × 20 = x × 40
⇒ 40 = 40x
⇒ x = 1

∴ বড় গিয়ারটি 1 বার ঘুরবে।

সঠিক উত্তর: ক) 1 বার

নোট: পরস্পর সংযুক্ত দুটি গিয়ার বিপরীত দিকে ঘোরে।

Anatomy.question: ৯৪) When is oogenesis completed?
Anatomy.exp: Explanation: Oogenesis begins before birth. Primary oocytes arrest in prophase I until puberty. After meiosis I, the secondary oocyte arrests in metaphase II. Meiosis II is completed only after fertilisation, forming the mature ovum.

Anatomy.question: ৩) Which is the most superficial layer of the epidermis?
Anatomy.exp:
Stratum corneum is the outermost layer of the epidermis.

More About the Epidermis

• Superficial → Deep
 • Stratum corneum
 • Stratum lucidum (thick skin only)
 • Stratum granulosum
 • Stratum spinosum
 • Stratum basale

Anatomy.question: ৬১) Which blood vessels are the principal site of vascular resistance?
Anatomy.exp: Arterioles are the principal resistance vessels because their small radius and adjustable smooth-muscle tone allow them to regulate systemic vascular resistance, blood pressure, and tissue blood flow.

Anatomy.question: ৫৩) What is the principal site of sperm storage?
Anatomy.exp:
The epididymis, particularly its tail, is the principal site for sperm maturation and storage.

Specific functions of Male Reproductive System
• Testis → Sperm production
• Epididymis → Sperm maturation and storage
• Vas deferens → Sperm transport
• Seminal vesicle → Fructose-rich seminal fluid

Anatomy.question: ৭৭) What is the principal content of Calot’s triangle?
Anatomy.exp:
The cystic artery is the principal vascular structure within Calot’s triangle.

More About Calot’s Triangle

• Boundaries
  • Medial → Common hepatic duct
  • Lateral → Cystic duct
  • Superior → Inferior surface of liver

• Contents
  • Cystic artery
  • Cystic lymph node 

• Clinical importance
  • Identified during cholecystectomy
  • Helps safely identify the cystic artery and cystic duct before ligation.

Anatomy.question: ৫১) Which cell forms the myelin sheath in the PNS?
Anatomy.exp:
Schwann cells form the myelin sheath of peripheral nerves.

More About Myelin Sheath
PNS myelination is carried out by Schwann cells, with each cell myelinating one segment of a single axon.
CNS myelination is carried out by oligodendrocytes, with each cell capable of myelinating segments of multiple axons.

Anatomy.question: ৪৮) Which of the following structures of the eye is avascular?
Anatomy.exp:
The cornea is avascular and receives nutrients mainly by diffusion from the tear film, aqueous humour, and limbal vessels.

• Avascular → Cornea, lens, vitreous body

Anatomy.question: ১৭৩) Which blood cell lacks mitochondria?
Anatomy.exp: Mature erythrocytes lack mitochondria and therefore depend entirely on anaerobic glycolysis for ATP production.

Anatomy.question: ১৮৬) Which structure is known as the “policeman of the abdomen”?
Anatomy.exp:
The greater omentum is called the “policeman of the abdomen” because it tends to migrate toward and help contain areas of intra-abdominal inflammation.

• Greater omentum → “Policeman of the abdomen”
• Vermiform appendix → “Abdominal tonsil”
• Palatine tonsil → “Gatekeeper of the respiratory and digestive tracts”

Anatomy.question: ৮৩) Which is a purely sensory cranial nerve nucleus?
Anatomy.exp: Nucleus tractus solitarius (NTS) is a sensory nucleus receiving visceral and taste afferents from CN VII, IX and X.

Anatomy.question: ২৮) What is the most important factor maintaining the position of the uterus?
Anatomy.exp:
The pelvic floor muscles, particularly levator ani, provide the main dynamic support for the uterus.

More About Uterine Support
• Main support → Pelvic floor (levator ani)
• Key fascial support → Transverse cervical (cardinal) ligaments
• Additional support → Uterosacral and pubocervical ligaments
• Broad ligament → Mainly a peritoneal fold; not a major supporting structure

Anatomy.question: ৫) Which cells secrete pulmonary surfactant?
Anatomy.exp:
Type II pneumocytes secrete pulmonary surfactant, which reduces alveolar surface tension and prevents alveolar collapse.

More About Alveolar Cells

• Type I pneumocytes → Gas exchange
• Type II pneumocytes → Surfactant secretion + alveolar epithelial repair
• Alveolar macrophages → Phagocytosis and removal of particles/debris
• Goblet cells → Mucus secretion in conducting airways

Physiology.question: ৯৯) Which part of the adrenal gland produces glucocorticoids?
Physiology.exp:
Glucocorticoids (mainly cortisol) are produced by the zona fasciculata of the adrenal cortex.

More About the Adrenal Gland
• Adrenal cortex → GFR
 • Glomerulosa → Aldosterone
 • Fasciculata → Cortisol
 • Reticularis → Androgens

• Adrenal medulla → Catecholamines
 • Adrenaline (epinephrine)
 • Noradrenaline (norepinephrine)

• Zona glomerulosa: regulated mainly by angiotensin II and serum K⁺, rather than the hypothalamic–pituitary axis.

Physiology.question: ৫০) First heart sound corresponds most closely to which ECG event?
Physiology.exp:
• QRS begins → Ventricular depolarisation

• S1 → Mitral + tricuspid valve closure
• Therefore, S1 occurs just after the onset of QRS.

Physiology.question: ১৭১) Which endocrine secretion is under direct hypothalamic–pituitary control?
Physiology.exp:
Testosterone is regulated by the hypothalamic–pituitary–gonadal axis: GnRH → LH → Leydig cells → testosterone.

Regulations:
• PTH → Serum ionised Ca²⁺
• Aldosterone → Angiotensin II + serum K⁺
• Insulin → Blood glucose
• Testosterone → GnRH → LH → Leydig cells

Physiology.question: ৬৭) Which of the following is the most important excitatory neurotransmitter?
Physiology.exp:
Glutamate is the major excitatory neurotransmitter in the CNS.

More About Neurotransmitters

• Glutamate → Major excitatory neurotransmitter
• GABA → Major inhibitory neurotransmitter in the brain
• Glycine → Major inhibitory neurotransmitter in the spinal cord

Physiology.question: ১৩৪) What is the renal clearance of glucose under normal conditions?
Physiology.exp: Renal clearance is the volume of plasma completely cleared of a substance by the kidneys per unit time. Glucose clearance is normally zero because filtered glucose is completely reabsorbed in the proximal tubule.

Physiology.question: ১৫২) Which organelle contains catalase?
Physiology.exp:
Peroxisomes contain catalase, which breaks down hydrogen peroxide (H₂O₂).

More About Lysosome

• Function → Intracellular digestion
• Enzymes → Acid hydrolases
• Breaks down → Cellular debris and damaged organelles

More About Peroxisome

• Function → Oxidation and detoxification
• Enzymes → Oxidases + catalase
• Catalase → Breaks down H₂O₂
• Key role → Very-long-chain fatty acid oxidation

Physiology.question: ৮২) Which of the following is the most common type of hypoxia?
Physiology.exp:
Hypoxic hypoxia is the most common type and occurs when arterial PaO₂ is reduced, resulting in reduced oxygen availability to tissues.

More About Hypoxia

Definition
• Hypoxia → Inadequate oxygen availability or utilisation at the tissue level.

Types of Hypoxia

• Hypoxic hypoxia → ↓ PaO₂
  Examples: High altitude, respiratory disease

• Anaemic hypoxia → ↓ O₂-carrying capacity
  Examples: Anaemia, carbon monoxide poisoning

• Stagnant hypoxia → ↓ Tissue blood flow
  Examples: Heart failure, shock

• Histotoxic hypoxia → Impaired cellular utilisation of O₂
  Example: Cyanide poisoning

Physiology.question: ১২৬) Which statement about renin is correct?
Physiology.exp:
Renin is produced by JG cells and acts on angiotensinogen, which is produced mainly by the liver.

More About Renin

Production
• Produced by JG cells of the kidney.

Stimuli for Renin Release
• Decreased renal perfusion pressure
• Decreased NaCl delivery to macula densa
• Increased sympathetic stimulation via β₁ receptors

RAAS Pathway
• Renin → Angiotensinogen → Angiotensin I
• ACE → Angiotensin I → Angiotensin II
• Angiotensin II → Aldosterone + ADH + vasoconstriction

Main Functions
• Increases blood pressure
• Promotes Na⁺ and water retention
• Helps restore renal perfusion pressure

Bio-chemistry.question: ১১২) Which glucose transporter is insulin-dependent?
Bio-chemistry.exp:
GLUT4 is insulin-dependent and is found mainly in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue.

More About GLUTs
• GLUT1 → RBCs, blood–brain barrier
• GLUT2 → Liver, pancreatic β-cells
• GLUT3 → Brain
• GLUT4 → Skeletal muscle, adipose tissue → insulin-dependent

Bio-chemistry.question: ৬) What is the basic structural unit of DNA?
Bio-chemistry.exp: A nucleotide is the basic structural unit of DNA and consists of a nitrogenous base, pentose sugar, and phosphate group.

Bio-chemistry.question: ৩২) Which is the main metabolic fuel of the heart under normal conditions?
Bio-chemistry.exp: The heart primarily uses fatty acids for energy under normal resting conditions, although it can also use glucose, lactate and ketone bodies.

Bio-chemistry.question: ৮৯) Which ketone body is mainly responsible for metabolic acidosis in diabetic ketoacidosis?
Bio-chemistry.exp:
β-Hydroxybutyrate is the predominant ketoacid responsible for the metabolic acidosis of diabetic ketoacidosis.

More About Ketone Bodies

• β-Hydroxybutyrate → Major ketoacid in DKA
• Acetoacetate → Ketoacid contributing to acidosis
• Acetone → Volatile, non-acidic ketone body responsible for fruity breath

Bio-chemistry.question: ১০৮) Which nutrient provides the greatest energy yield per gram?
Bio-chemistry.exp:
Fat provides 9 kcal/g, compared with 4 kcal/g for carbohydrate and protein.

More About Energy Yield

• Fat → 9 kcal/g
• Alcohol → 7 kcal/g
• Carbohydrate → 4 kcal/g
• Protein → 4 kcal/g

Pharmacology.question: ৪৭) Which drug reverses the anticoagulant effect of warfarin?
Pharmacology.exp:
Vitamin K₁ reverses warfarin-induced anticoagulation by restoring synthesis of vitamin K–dependent clotting factors.

Antidotes to Remember
Warfarin → Vitamin K
Heparin → Protamine sulfate
Opioids → Naloxone
Benzodiazepines → Flumazenil
Organophosphorus poisoning → Atropine + Pralidoxime
Paracetamol → N-acetylcysteine

Pharmacology.question: ২৪) Which drug can cause premature closure of the ductus arteriosus?
Pharmacology.exp:
Indomethacin, an NSAID that inhibits prostaglandin synthesis, can cause premature closure of the ductus arteriosus.

• Clinical use of indomethacin → Closure of a patent ductus arteriosus (PDA)

Pharmacology.question: ১১৯) Which antipsychotic drug is most strongly associated with agranulocytosis?
Pharmacology.exp:
Clozapine can cause serious agranulocytosis, requiring regular blood-count monitoring.

More About side effects of Antipsychotics 
• Clozapine → Agranulocytosis + lowest EPS
• Haloperidol → Highest EPS
• Olanzapine → Weight gain
• Risperidone → Hyperprolactinaemia

Pharmacology.question: ১৩) Which term refers to the maximum effect a drug can produce?
Pharmacology.exp:
Efficacy is the maximum effect a drug can produce, whereas potency refers to the dose required to produce an effect.

More About Drug Action

• Efficacy → Maximum effect
• Potency → Dose required for an effect
• Affinity → Receptor-binding ability
• Bioavailability → Fraction reaching systemic circulation

Pharmacology.question: ১৮০) Which of the following drugs has a low therapeutic index?
Pharmacology.exp:
Digoxin has a narrow therapeutic index, so small changes in dose or plasma concentration may cause toxicity.

More About Therapeutic Index
• Low therapeutic index → Requires close monitoring
 • Methotrexate
 • Aminoglycosides
 • Cyclosporine
 • Digoxin
 • Phenytoin
 • Valproate
 • Lithium
 • Warfarin
 • Tricyclic antidepressants
 • Theophylline

• Relatively high therapeutic index → Wider safety margin
 • Penicillins and many β-lactam antibiotics
 • Thiazide diuretics
 • Diazepam
 • Clonazepam
 • Paracetamol at therapeutic doses

Forensic Medicine & Toxicology.question: ১৮) Which preservative is most commonly used in forensic specimens?
Forensic Medicine & Toxicology.exp: Saturated solution of common salt is the most commonly used preservative in the forensic.

Forensic Medicine & Toxicology.question: ১০৭) Which finding is characteristic of ante-mortem hanging?
Forensic Medicine & Toxicology.exp: Dribbling of saliva from the angle of the mouth is a characteristic sign of hanging.

Forensic Medicine & Toxicology.question: ১১৮) Which of the following is an example of criminal negligence by a doctor?
Forensic Medicine & Toxicology.option2: Wrong diagnosis due to lack of knowledge
Forensic Medicine & Toxicology.exp:
Performing an illegal abortion is a classic example of criminal negligence.

More About Medical Negligence

• Civil negligence → Wrong diagnosis, negligent procedure, failure of consent, premature discharge
• Criminal negligence → Illegal abortion, gross anaesthesia error, wrong surgery, retained foreign body, serious drug error

Forensic Medicine & Toxicology.question: ৮৪) Which is the best single bone for sex determination?
Forensic Medicine & Toxicology.exp:
• Pelvis → Best single bone for sex determination
• Female pelvis → Wider, shallower, broader subpubic angle
• Male pelvis → Narrower, deeper, narrower subpubic angle

More About Sex Determination

• Pelvis → Most reliable
• Skull → Second most useful
• Long bones → Less reliable than pelvis and skull

Forensic Medicine & Toxicology.question: ১১০) Which branch of forensic medicine deals with the study of legal aspects of death?
Forensic Medicine & Toxicology.exp:
• Thanatology → Study of death and its legal/medicolegal aspects
• Forensic ballistics → Firearms and ammunition
• Dactylography → Fingerprints
• Forensic pathology → Death, disease and injury from a medicolegal perspective

Community Medicine and Public Health.question: ৬৫) Which study is most appropriate for determining the prevalence of a disease?
Community Medicine and Public Health.exp:
Cross-sectional studies measure disease prevalence at a specific point or period in time.

More About Study Designs
• Cross-sectional → Prevalence
• Cohort → Incidence
• RCT → Treatment efficacy

Community Medicine and Public Health.question: ১১) Which type of immunity is most important in preventing epidemics?
Community Medicine and Public Health.exp: Herd immunity reduces transmission of infection within a population and helps prevent epidemics.

Community Medicine and Public Health.question: ১৫১) Which type of vaccine is the HPV vaccine in Bangladesh?
Community Medicine and Public Health.exp:
The HPV vaccine is a recombinant subunit vaccine containing L1 protein virus-like particles (VLPs).

More About Vaccine Types

Live Attenuated Vaccines
• BCG
• MMR
• Oral polio vaccine (OPV)
• Varicella
• Yellow fever

Inactivated / Killed Vaccines
• Inactivated polio vaccine (IPV)
• Hepatitis A
• Rabies
• Inactivated influenza vaccine

Subunit / Recombinant Vaccines
• HPV → L1 VLP vaccine
• Hepatitis B → Recombinant HBsAg
• Acellular pertussis → Purified bacterial components

Toxoid Vaccines
• Diphtheria
• Tetanus

Conjugate Vaccines
• Hib
• Pneumococcal
• Meningococcal

Community Medicine and Public Health.question: ১১৬) How does the combined oral contraceptive pill mainly act?
Community Medicine and Public Health.exp:
Mechanisms of Common Contraceptives
• Combined OCP → Ovulation suppression
• Progestin-only pill → Cervical mucus thickening
• Copper IUCD → Spermicide
• Condom → Barrier to sperm
• DMPA + Implant → Ovulation suppression

Community Medicine and Public Health.question: ১৮৯) Which indicator is most commonly used to measure the health status of a population?
Community Medicine and Public Health.exp: Infant mortality rate is a widely used indicator of the health status and socioeconomic conditions of a population.

Pathology.question: ৮৮) Which of the following is not a cellular adaptation?
Pathology.exp:
Anaplasia refers to loss of cellular differentiation and is a characteristic feature of malignant neoplasia, not a cellular adaptation.

More About Cellular Adaptation

• Atrophy → Decrease in cell size
• Hypertrophy → Increase in cell size
• Hyperplasia → Increase in cell number
• Metaplasia → Reversible replacement of one mature cell type by another

Pathology.question: ১৪৭) Which feature is most characteristic of basal cell carcinoma?
Pathology.exp: Basal cell carcinoma is locally invasive but metastasizes very rarely.

Pathology.question: ৮৫) Where does atherosclerosis mainly occur?
Pathology.exp: Atherosclerosis mainly affects large and medium-sized arteries. LDL enters the arterial intima, where it can undergo oxidative modification; oxidised LDL is readily taken up by macrophages, promoting foam-cell formation and atherosclerotic plaque.

Pathology.question: ১৭৭) Which pathological finding is characteristic of acute rheumatic fever?
Pathology.exp:
Aschoff bodies are the characteristic histological lesion of acute rheumatic fever.

More About the Findings

• Aschoff bodies → Acute rheumatic fever
• Reed–Sternberg cells → Hodgkin lymphoma
• Councilman bodies → Viral hepatitis
• Mallory bodies → Alcoholic liver disease

Pathology.question: ৪৪) What is the most important factor predisposing to venous thrombosis?
Pathology.exp:
Blood stasis is the major predisposing factor for venous thrombosis, particularly with prolonged immobilisation.

More About Venous Thrombosis

• Virchow’s triad
 • Stasis
 • Endothelial injury
 • Hypercoagulability

• Venous thrombosis → Mainly stasis + hypercoagulability

• Arterial thrombosis → More strongly associated with endothelial injury.

Microbiology.question: ৫৪) Which of the following is a hallmark of primary syphilis?
Microbiology.exp:
Clinical Features of Syphilis
* Primary
   • Painless chancre 
   • Painless regional lymphadenopathy

* Secondary
   • Generalised rash → palms & soles
   • Condyloma lata
   • Gun-metal grey appearance
   • Generalised lymphadenopathy

* Tertiary
   • Gumma
   • Cardiovascular syphilis
   • Neurosyphilis → Tabes dorsalis

Microbiology.question: ৭১) Which is the most common mechanism of antibiotic resistance?
Microbiology.exp:
Enzymatic drug inactivation is a major mechanism of antibiotic resistance. Bacteria produce enzymes that destroy or chemically modify the antibiotic, making it ineffective.

More About Antibiotic Resistance

• β-lactamase → Breaks β-lactam antibiotics
• Altered target → Prevents effective drug binding
• Reduced permeability → Decreases drug entry
• Efflux pump → Removes drug from the bacterial cell

Microbiology.question: ১৩৯) Which organism is the most common cause of UTI?
Microbiology.exp: E. coli is the most common cause of urinary tract infection.

Microbiology.question: ৯৩) Which of the following is an example of Type II hypersensitivity?
Microbiology.exp:
Type II hypersensitivity is mediated by IgG or IgM antibodies directed against cell-surface or extracellular-matrix antigens.

More About Hypersensitivity
• Type I → IgE → Anaphylaxis, allergic rhinitis
• Type II → IgG/IgM → Goodpasture syndrome, autoimmune haemolytic anaemia,
• Type III → Immune complexes → SLE, rheumatoid arthritis, serum sickness
• Type IV → T cells mediated → Contact dermatitis, tuberculosis skin reaction

- Hashimoto thyroiditis-এর pathogenesis predominantly T-cell mediated autoimmune destruction, অর্থাৎ Type IV mechanism গুরুত্বপূর্ণ।

Microbiology.question: ১১৭) Which bacterial component can cause profound shock?
Microbiology.exp: LPS, particularly its lipid A component, is the endotoxin of Gram-negative bacteria and can trigger massive cytokine release, leading to profound hypotension and septic shock.

Medicine.question: ১৭০) Non-pitting oedema is classically seen in:
Medicine.exp:
Filariasis can cause lymphoedema, resulting in non-pitting oedema due to obstruction of lymphatic drainage.

More About Oedema

• Lymphoedema → Non-pitting
• Myxoedema → Non-pitting
• Heart failure → Pitting
• Nephrotic syndrome → Pitting

Medicine.question: ১৮৭) Which condition is commonly assessed using the DAS28 score?
Medicine.exp:
DAS28 is a disease activity score used in rheumatoid arthritis to assess disease activity.

More About Common Clinical Scores

• Sepsis → SOFA score
• Pneumonia → CURB-65
• Chronic liver disease → Child-Pugh score
• Chronic kidney disease → KDIGO staging / eGFR
• Rheumatoid arthritis → DAS28

Medicine.question: ১৪২) What is the usual duration of anti-TB treatment for primary pulmonary tuberculosis?
Medicine.exp:
Standard drug-susceptible pulmonary TB is treated for 6 months: 2 months of HRZE, followed by 4 months of HR.

More About Anti-TB Treatment

• Intensive phase → 2 months: H + R + Z + E
• Continuation phase → 4 months: H + R
• Total → 6 months

Medicine.question: ৩৫) Which is the characteristic feature of scabies?
Medicine.exp:
• Burrows → Characteristic feature of scabies

• Cause → Sarcoptes scabiei infestation
• Typical site → Finger webs, wrists, axillae, genital area
• symptom → Intense nocturnal pruritus

Medicine.question: ১৭৯) Absent “a” wave in JVP is found in which condition?
Medicine.exp:
JVP = Jugular Venous Pressure

• a wave: Right atrial contraction
• Atrial fibrillation: No coordinated atrial contraction
• Result: a wave is absent

Important JVP Findings

• Giant a wave: Pulmonary hypertension, pulmonary stenosis, tricuspid stenosis
• Cannon a wave: Complete heart block, ventricular tachycardia
• Large v wave: Tricuspid regurgitation

Medicine.question: ৯৫) What is the pathognomonic sign of measles?
Medicine.exp:
• Koplik spots → Pathognomonic of measles
• Site → Buccal mucosa, opposite the molars
• Appearance → Tiny white/blue-white spots on a red background

Medicine.question: ৬৩) Which cardiac biomarker is commonly used to detect heart failure?
Medicine.exp:
• NT-proBNP
• Released in response to ventricular wall stress
• Elevated in heart failure
• Used to support the diagnosis of heart failure

More About Cardiac Biomarkers

• Troponin I / T → Most specific marker of myocardial injury

• CK-MB → Useful for detecting recurrent MI

• Myoglobin → Early marker of myocardial injury; non-specific

Medicine.question: ১৩৬) Which of the following is the most specific laboratory marker for iron deficiency?
Medicine.exp: Low serum ferritin indicates depleted iron stores and is the most specific routine marker of iron deficiency. However, ferritin may be falsely normal or raised in inflammation.

Medicine.question: ১৫) Which metabolic condition is not usually associated with severe diarrhoea?
Medicine.exp:
• Severe diarrhoea → Loss of HCO₃⁻, K⁺ and Na⁺ in stool
• Result → Normal-anion-gap metabolic acidosis + hypokalaemia + hyponatraemia
• Metabolic alkalosis → Usually associated with vomiting / nasogastric suction due to HCl loss

Medicine.question: ২১) During BP measurement, which Korotkoff phase indicates the systolic blood pressure?
Medicine.exp:
Phase I is the first appearance of Korotkoff sounds and indicates systolic blood pressure.

More About Korotkoff Sounds

• Phase I → Systolic BP
• Phase II → Swishing sound
• Phase III → Loud, clear sounds
• Phase IV → Muffling of sounds
• Phase V → Disappearance → Diastolic BP

Medicine.question: ৪৫) Which of the following is a warning sign of dengue fever?
৫৭) Which X-ray finding is characteristic of thalassaemia major?
Medicine.exp:
• Thalassaemia major → Marrow expansion due to chronic haemolysis
• Skull X-ray → Hair-on-end / crew-cut appearance
• Long bones → Cortical thinning and expansion
• Other finding → “Chipmunk facies” due to maxillary marrow expansion

Medicine.question: ২৬) All of the following are causes of thrombosis with thrombocytopenia, except :
Medicine.exp: ITP causes isolated thrombocytopenia due to immune-mediated platelet destruction, but thrombosis is not a typical feature. In contrast, HUS, TTP and DIC cause thrombocytopenia associated with microvascular thrombosis.

Medicine.question: ২০০) Which is the most effective anti-obesity drug?
Medicine.exp:
Tirzepatide is the most effective among these options, producing approximately 25% weight loss.

More About Anti-obesity Drugs

• Orlistat → Pancreatic lipase inhibitor → 3–5% weight loss
• Liraglutide → GLP-1 receptor agonist → ~5–10% weight loss
• Semaglutide → GLP-1 receptor agonist → ~15% weight loss
• Tirzepatide → Dual agonist (GIP + GLP-1 receptor agonist) → ~25% weight loss

Medicine.question: ১২৫) Which antidiabetic drug is most associated with weight gain?
Medicine.exp:
Insulin commonly causes weight gain, whereas metformin, empagliflozin and semaglutide are generally weight-reducing or weight-neutral.

Weight Effects of Antidiabetic Drugs

Weight Gain
• Insulin
• Sulfonylureas
• Pioglitazone

Weight Loss
• GLP-1 receptor agonists → Semaglutide, liraglutide
• SGLT2 inhibitors → Empagliflozin, dapagliflozin

Weight Neutral
• Metformin → Usually weight-neutral / modest weight loss
• DPP-4 inhibitors → Weight-neutral

Medicine.question: ৭৫) What is the most common cause of chronic kidney disease (CKD)?
Medicine.exp:
Diabetes mellitus is the leading cause of CKD worldwide, mainly due to diabetic kidney disease.

Key Point

• Most common cause of CKD → Diabetes mellitus
• Major contributor → Hypertension

Medicine.question: ১৭৫) Which condition is most likely to cause low radioactive iodine uptake in thyrotoxicosis?
Medicine.exp:
Subacute thyroiditis causes release of preformed thyroid hormones from damaged thyroid follicles, so the thyroid does not actively synthesise excess hormone, resulting in low radioactive iodine uptake.

Radioactive Iodine Uptake

Low Uptake
• Subacute / silent / postpartum thyroiditis
• Exogenous thyroid hormone

High Uptake
• Graves’ disease → Diffuse uptake
• Toxic multinodular goitre → Patchy uptake
• Toxic adenoma → Focal uptake

Surgery.question: ১৬) Which of the following sign is associated with acute pancreatitis?
Surgery.exp:
• Cullen’s sign → Periumbilical bluish discoloration due to intra-abdominal bleeding; classically associated with severe acute pancreatitis

• Grey Turner sign → Flank bruising; severe acute pancreatitis
• Murphy’s sign → Acute cholecystitis
• McBurney’s sign → Acute appendicitis

Surgery.question: ১৬৪) Which of the following is an example of a colloidal solution?
Surgery.exp:
Hydroxyethyl starch (HES) is a colloidal plasma-volume expander containing large molecules that exert oncotic pressure.

Common IV Fluids

Colloids
• Hydroxyethyl starch
• Gelatin solutions
• Albumin
• Dextran

Crystalloids
• Normal saline
• Ringer’s lactate
• 5% dextrose
• 3% NaCl

Surgery.question: ১১৫) Which incision is most commonly used for open appendicectomy?
Surgery.exp:
• Gridiron → Classical, commonly used for appendicectomy
• Lanz → Cosmetic skin-crease incision for appendicectomy
• Kocher → Cholecystectomy
• Rutherford Morrison → Wider exposure; muscle-cutting incision

Surgery.question: ১২) Which investigation best confirms achalasia?
Surgery.exp:
Oesophageal manometry is the gold-standard confirmatory test for achalasia, demonstrating impaired LES relaxation and absent normal peristalsis.

Key Point:
• Manometry → Confirms achalasia
• Barium swallow → Bird-beak appearance
• Endoscopy → Excludes mechanical obstruction / pseudoachalasia

Surgery.question: ৪১) After circumcision, bleeding most commonly occurs from which artery?
Surgery.exp:
The frenular artery, a branch of the dorsal penile artery, is an important source of bleeding following circumcision.

Common Surgical Procedures — Important Arterial Injury
• Cholecystectomy → Cystic artery
• Hernia repair → Inferior epigastric vessels
• Circumcision → Frenular artery
• Appendicectomy → Appendicular artery

Surgery.question: ৪০) Which is the most common site of perforation in peptic ulcer disease?
Surgery.exp:
Duodenal ulcer, particularly on the anterior wall of the first part of the duodenum, is the commonest site of peptic ulcer perforation.

Important Related Sites

• Gastric ulcer → Commonly lesser curvature
• Gastric cancer → Commonly distal stomach, especially the antrum
• Perforation → Anterior duodenal ulcer
• Bleeding → Posterior duodenal ulcer → gastroduodenal artery involvement

Surgery.question: ১৯০) Which tumour marker is commonly associated with breast cancer?
Surgery.exp:
CA 15-3 is commonly associated with breast cancer, mainly for monitoring treatment and recurrence, rather than screening.

Other Common Tumour Markers

• CA 15-3 → Breast cancer
• CA-125 → Ovarian cancer
• CA 19-9 → Pancreatic cancer
• AFP → Hepatocellular carcinoma
• CEA → Colorectal cancer
• PSA → Prostate cancer
• Calcitonin → Medullary thyroid carcinoma
• β-hCG → Choriocarcinoma / testicular germ-cell tumour

Surgery.question: ১০১) Which clinical sign indicates decompensated shock?
Surgery.exp:
Decompensated shock occurs when compensatory mechanisms fail, resulting in hypotension and inadequate tissue perfusion.

Compensated Shock
Shock is present, but compensation temporarily maintains blood pressure.

Features:
• Tachycardia
• Narrow pulse pressure
• Cool, clammy peripheries
• Blood pressure usually maintained

Decompensated Shock
Compensation fails, resulting in hypotension and worsening tissue hypoperfusion.

Features:
• Hypotension
• Worsening tissue hypoperfusion
• Restlessness or confusion

Remember: Normal blood pressure does not exclude shock.

Surgery.question: ৯০) Which is the most common organism causing osteomyelitis?
Surgery.exp:
Staphylococcus aureus is the most common causative organism of osteomyelitis, especially in haematogenous and contiguous infections.

Important Organisms

• Osteomyelitis → Staphylococcus aureus
• Sickle cell disease → Salmonella
• Puncture wound through shoe → Pseudomonas aeruginosa
• IV drug use → Staphylococcus aureus

Surgery.question: ৬৪) Which is the earliest symptom of acute intestinal obstruction?
Surgery.exp:
Colicky abdominal pain is usually the earliest symptom, caused by increased peristalsis against the obstruction.

Important Clinical Features of Intestinal Obstruction

• Earliest symptom: Colicky abdominal pain
• Small bowel / proximal obstruction: Early, prominent vomiting
• Large bowel / distal obstruction: Prominent constipation + abdominal distension
• Later: Absolute constipation / obstipation
• Sudden severe continuous pain: Strangulation / ischaemia

Surgery.question: ৭০) Which nerve is most commonly injured during thyroidectomy?
Surgery.exp: Recurrent laryngeal nerve injury is an important complication of thyroidectomy and may cause hoarseness or vocal cord paralysis.

Surgery.question: ১১১) Which is the most common cause of secondary haemorrhage after surgery?
Surgery.exp: Wound infection can cause secondary haemorrhage by eroding blood vessels, typically occurring several days after surgery.

Surgery.question: ৭২) Which is the key parameter to monitor while resuscitating a burn patient?
Surgery.exp:
Urine output is the key bedside parameter for assessing the adequacy of fluid resuscitation in a major burn patient. It reflects renal perfusion and overall response to fluid therapy.

Burn Resuscitation : 

• Target urine output in adults: ≥ 0.5 mL/kg/hour

• Example: A 70-kg adult should produce at least 35 mL urine/hour.

Surgery.question: ১৩৮) Which is a common complication of blood transfusion?
Surgery.exp: Hyperkalaemia can occur after transfusion, particularly with large-volume or stored blood transfusion, due to potassium leakage from stored red cells.

Surgery.question: ১৬২) Charcot’s biliary triad is classically associated with which of the following?
Surgery.option4: Carcinoma of the head of pancreas
Surgery.exp: Charcot’s biliary triad consists of fever, jaundice, and right upper quadrant pain and is classically associated with acute cholangitis.

Surgery.question: ১৫৯) What is the most commonly used method for inguinal hernia repair?
Surgery.exp: Lichtenstein tension-free mesh repair is the commonly used open surgical technique for inguinal hernia repair.

Surgery.question: ১০৪) Which clinical feature is most characteristic of gas gangrene?
Surgery.exp: Crepitus due to gas production within the soft tissues is a characteristic clinical feature of gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis).

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ৯৮) What is the most common cause of vaginal discharge ?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp:
Physiological vaginal discharge is the commonest cause of vaginal discharge. It is usually clear/white, non-offensive, and not associated with itching, irritation, or pain.

Important Point

• Overall vaginal discharge → Physiological
• Commonest infective cause → Bacterial vaginosis

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ১৬৬) A 29-year-old woman is being evaluated for infertility. Which investigation confirms ovulation?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp:
A day 21 (mid-luteal) serum progesterone confirms that ovulation has occurred.

Remember: 
• Confirm ovulation → Day 21 serum progesterone
• Predict ovulation → Urinary LH surge test

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ২৫) What is the leading gynaecological cause of death worldwide?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp:
Cervical cancer is a major cause of gynaecological cancer mortality worldwide, particularly in settings with limited screening and HPV vaccination.

Key Point:
• Leading gynaecological cancer killer worldwide → Cervical cancer

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ২) What is the hallmark feature of inevitable abortion?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp:
Inevitable abortion is characterized by vaginal bleeding with an open cervical os, indicating that continuation of pregnancy is no longer possible.

Key Point

• Threatened abortion: Vaginal bleeding + closed cervical os
• Inevitable abortion: Vaginal bleeding + open cervical os
• Other features: Lower abdominal pain, backache, and watery vaginal discharge may occur, but they are not diagnostic features.

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ১৯২) Which immunoglobulin is transferred across the placenta?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp:
IgG is the only major immunoglobulin that crosses the placenta, providing passive immunity to the fetus.

IgG1 → Most efficient placental transfer

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ১৯৭) What is the most common clinical feature of pelvic inflammatory disease ?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp: Lower abdominal/pelvic pain is the most common presenting feature of PID, often associated with bilateral lower abdominal tenderness and cervical motion tenderness.

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ১৬০) Which is the most common cause of maternal death in eclampsia?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp: Cerebral haemorrhage is a major cause of maternal death in eclampsia, resulting from severe hypertension and cerebral vascular injury.

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ১৭৪) What is the characteristic clinical feature of amniotic fluid embolism?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp: Cyanosis is a characteristic feature of amniotic fluid embolism due to acute respiratory compromise and hypoxaemia.

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ৫৮) Which fetal abnormality is classically associated with oligohydramnios?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp: Fetal renal agenesis causes markedly reduced fetal urine production, resulting in severe oligohydramnios.

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ৪) Which is the most common cause of primary postpartum haemorrhage (PPH)?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp:
Uterine atony is the most common cause of primary PPH due to failure of the uterus to contract effectively after delivery.

Key Point

• Primary PPH → Uterine atony is the most common cause
• Secondary PPH → Retained products of conception is a common cause

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ৩০) Which antihypertensive drug is contraindicated in pregnancy?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp:
Losartan, an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB), is contraindicated in pregnancy because it can cause fetal renal injury, oligohydramnios, and fetal death.

Key Point:
• Pregnancy → Avoid ACE inhibitors and ARBs
• Preferred → Labetalol, nifedipine, methyldopa

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ৩৮) Which is the most common symptom of endometriosis?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp: Endometriosis classically causes severe secondary dysmenorrhoea, often associated with chronic pelvic pain and dyspareunia.

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ৮০) What is the most common cause of spontaneous abortion in the first trimester?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp:
Fetal chromosomal abnormalities are the most common cause of first-trimester spontaneous abortion.

Remember:

• First trimester: Chromosomal abnormalities
• Cervical incompetence: Painless second-trimester cervical dilatation and pregnancy loss
• APS: Recurrent pregnancy loss ± thrombosis
• Diabetes: Increases miscarriage risk, but is not the commonest cause.

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ১৭৮) Which is the immediate first step in the Active Management of the Third Stage of Labour (AMTSL)?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.option1: Clamping and cutting of the umbilical cord
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp:
Oxytocin 10 IU IM is administered immediately after birth to promote uterine contraction and reduce postpartum haemorrhage.

Third Stage of Labour: From delivery of the baby until delivery of the placenta and membranes.

AMTSL Steps
• Oxytocin 10 IU IM
• Delayed cord clamping and cutting
• Controlled cord traction for placental delivery
• Uterine fundal massage and assessment of uterine tone after placental delivery

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ১০৯) What is the most common fetal complication of untreated gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM)?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp:
Maternal hyperglycaemia → fetal hyperglycaemia → fetal hyperinsulinaemia → increased fat and protein deposition → macrosomia.

GDM — Important Complications

Fetus
• Macrosomia
• Fetal growth abnormalities

During Delivery
• Shoulder dystocia
• Birth trauma
• Difficult/prolonged labour

Neonate
• Hypoglycaemia
• Respiratory distress
• Polycythaemia

Mother
• Pre-eclampsia
• Operative delivery
• Increased future risk of type 2 diabetes

Obstetrics and Gynaecology.question: ১৩৫) A 70-year-old multiparous woman presents with stress urinary incontinence. What is the appropriate first-line management?
Obstetrics and Gynaecology.exp:
Pelvic floor exercises are the first-line treatment for stress urinary incontinence.

Urinary Incontinence :

• Stress → Pelvic floor exercises
• Urge → Bladder retraining → Antimuscarinic drugs
• Overflow → Catheterisation → Treat obstruction
• Severe/refractory stress → Surgical repair
